From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <opark@acme-analytics.com>, platform@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME Analytics: throughput & latency anomaly — runbook, product asks, customer note

Team —

ACME flagged a sharp degradation this morning at ~08:50 PT. Key observations from their telemetry + our monitoring:
- 95th pct latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~420ms -> ~2.1s across the text-gen route (ACME dedicated pool).
- Sustained throughput drop ~40% at peak (requests queued; token throughput down).
- Error rates remain low (5xxs not spike), but tail latency is causing upstream backpressure on their workers.

I attached incident logs (incident_logs_20260220.zip) with trace snippets and runtime counters. ACME is asking for: immediate mitigation, ETA for full resolution, and whether this impacts their SLA. They called this urgent.

Immediate asks:
1) Triage owner for infra (Marissa) and runtime/model (Karthik).
2) Short-term mitigation options we can apply within 60-90m (fallback model, routing override, or runtime rollback).
3) Draft customer acknowledgement to send within 90m. I'll own customer comms once we have the mitigation and ETA.

Notes / hypotheses: we pushed kernel/runner changes to dedicated pools last night (rollout window 02:00-04:00). Possible correlation with increased kernel compile miss or scheduling pressure.

Please reply with: owner + what landing action you recommend in the next 60m.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
mobile: (555) 555-0181

On Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 09:12 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
>
> ACME flagged a sharp degradation this morning at ~08:50 PT. Key observations ...

Thanks, Dylan — I’ll take infra ownership. First pass findings:
- Cluster metrics show spike in GPU scheduler wait on dedicated-pool-acme-01 between 08:40-09:00. No node OOMs.
- Kernel compile cache misses increased ~3x coincident with latency spike.
- Autoscaler did not add nodes (pool at max_capacity = true).

Immediate mitigations I can execute now (if approved):
A) Increase pool capacity by bursting to reserved nodes (5-10m to spin up) — short-term throughput relief.
B) Temporarily move ACME traffic to a compatible fallback model variant (smaller) to remove runtime pressure — risk: quality drop.
C) Isolate ACME to a previously-known-good runtime build in an adjacent pool (requires Karthik to confirm build availability).

I will start A + smoke test concurrently. Karthik — can you validate option C (rollback image) and whether we can do a targeted swap for ACME only?

I’ll prepare a preliminary customer note and drop it into this thread for review within 45m.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 09:27 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Dylan — I’ll take infra ownership. First pass findings: ...

Quick tech summary from runtime side:
- After rolling the 02:00 runtime update we observed an increase in on-the-fly kernel-selection misses for certain seq-len distributions (seen in the logs Dylan attached).
- The new runtime does more aggressive kernel compilation on demand; in a cold working set this can cause latency spikes while cache warms. That aligns with Marissa's compile-miss observation.

Short-term options (technical):
1) Rollback dedicated-pool-acme to the previous runtime image (tags: runtime-v1.12.3) — low risk for customer-specific pool; requires a fast image swap and quick sanity checks (estimated 20-30m if we have reserved capacity).
2) Force a pre-warm compile pass to populate kernel cache for ACME patterns (non-invasive but may take 10-20m to stabilize).
3) Apply traffic-split to route ACME to a smaller quantized model for immediate latency relief (quality tradeoff).

I recommend option 1 + 2 in parallel: rollback the pool image to v1.12.3 while we trigger a targeted pre-warm job. Marissa — if you can burst capacity, I’ll coordinate the image swap. Hannah — need product sign-off for any customer-facing quality degradation (option 3) and for a short-term routing override capability request (see product ask below).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:02:05 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Analytics: throughput & latency anomaly — runbook, product asks, customer note

Thanks all — good triage. Approved actions:
- Approve runtime rollback to runtime-v1.12.3 for the ACME dedicated pool (Karthik + Marissa coordinate). Prioritize isolated swap to avoid broader rollout.
- Approve targeted kernel pre-warm job.
- Do NOT route ACME to a lower-quality model without explicit customer consent — Connor, include the option and impact in the customer note.

Product ask (short term / roadmap):
We need a small capability that allows operations to pin a customer's traffic to an alternate model or runtime variant via Console (routing override per-customer) with an emergency TTL. This is a single-feature toggle (on/off + TTL + reason) and should be scoped as a P1 hotfix to reduce future MOP time. Karthik — please capture a short tech spec to hand to PM/Eng on Monday; Hannah will own prioritization.

Customer messaging: send an acknowledgement now (Connor to draft). Promise: update within 2 hours with mitigation status and ETA for full resolution.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:18:30 -0800
Subject: [Redwood] Acknowledgement: ACME latency/throughput anomaly (we're investigating)

Oliver / ACME team —

Thanks for flagging this. We’ve identified elevated tail latency impacting your dedicated inference pool and are actively investigating root cause. Immediate steps we are taking:
- Isolating ACME pool for a fast runtime rollback to a known-good build; this is expected to restore tail latency for most requests.
- Running a kernel pre-warm to reduce on-demand compile latency.
- As a last resort, we will present a fallback model option (lower latency) if you prefer a faster but lower-quality short-term route. We will not switch without your approval.

What to expect now:
- Short acknowledgement from us (this email) — we will send a mitigation update within 2 hours.
- If we proceed with the runtime rollback, brief request routing impact may occur (few minutes) while we swap the pool image.

Requested from you: please reply if you prefer we proceed immediately with the runtime rollback OR if you want us to try a temporary model fallback first.

We apologize for the disruption — we’re committed to resolving this quickly and will keep you updated.

Connor O'Brien
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft)

Connor / Redwood —

Thanks for the quick acknowledgement. We prefer the runtime rollback if it restores quality and latency; fallback model is a last resort. Two asks from our side:
1) Please share expected impact numbers (p50/p95, throughput delta) after rollback so we can plan upstream workers.
2) Clarify whether this incident will be considered for SLA credit — our procurement team is on copy.

Appreciate the transparency. Waiting on your mitigation update.

Oliver Park

opark@acme-analytics.com
